title: Calm Habit Design Checklist v1.0
description: An open, machine-readable checklist for reviewing whether a digital habit tool preserves user agency, makes feedback legible and separates product mechanics from evidence of real-world outcomes.
methodology: Victor Laybats authored the checklist from Reef’s documented product boundaries and public methodology. Each item is written as a review question and an evidence request. The release does not score Reef or any competing product.
limitations: This is a normative design checklist, not a clinical instrument, controlled experiment, certification or proof that a habit will form. A product can satisfy a criterion and still be ineffective or unsuitable in a particular context. Reviewers should record the app version, platform, date and evidence they actually observed.

criteria.criterion: The user chooses the action being tracked.
criteria.rationale: Agency starts with a goal selected by the person, not inferred by the product.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Show where a user creates or selects the action.

criteria.criterion: The action can be described in observable terms.
criteria.rationale: Observable actions are easier to review than vague promises about identity or health.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Record the goal label, schedule and completion rule.

criteria.criterion: A goal can be edited, paused or removed.
criteria.rationale: Changing circumstances should not trap a person in an obsolete commitment.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Demonstrate the edit, pause and deletion controls.

criteria.criterion: The interface distinguishes user input from calculated progress.
criteria.rationale: People should know which facts they entered and which values the product derived.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Label a completion, a calculated count and any inferred status.

criteria.criterion: Decorative rewards are identifiable as product mechanics.
criteria.rationale: Animation and collectibles can motivate without being presented as scientific evidence.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Identify each decorative reward and the action that unlocks it.

criteria.criterion: Streak and completion calculations are explainable.
criteria.rationale: A visible calculation lets users understand resets, time zones and missed entries.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Document the calculation, reset rule and time-zone behavior.

criteria.criterion: A missed day has a clear return path.
criteria.rationale: Recovery supports continued use without turning one lapse into a disproportionate penalty.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Demonstrate the first session after a missed day.

criteria.criterion: Copy avoids shame, diagnosis and moral judgment.
criteria.rationale: A tracker should report product state without judging the person.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Review empty, lapse, reminder and cancellation messages.

criteria.criterion: Historical progress remains understandable after a break.
criteria.rationale: People need an accurate record even when continuity changes.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Inspect how gaps and prior completions are displayed.

criteria.criterion: Reminders are optional and controllable.
criteria.rationale: Notifications should support a chosen routine, not manufacture urgency.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Show opt-in, schedule, mute and disable controls.

criteria.criterion: The product works without manipulative countdowns or false scarcity.
criteria.rationale: Artificial urgency can displace the user’s goal with the product’s engagement target.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Review purchase, streak and reward prompts for time pressure.

criteria.criterion: Reduced-motion and interruption needs are considered.
criteria.rationale: Visual reward systems should remain usable when motion or repeated interruption is unwelcome.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Test system motion settings and notification-disabled use.

criteria.criterion: Social participation is optional.
criteria.rationale: Private self-tracking should not require public performance.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Complete the core workflow without adding contacts or posting.

criteria.criterion: Audience and visibility are clear before sharing.
criteria.rationale: Users need to know who can see a goal, completion or media item.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Capture the audience selector and resulting view.

criteria.criterion: Rankings and comparison do not redefine personal progress.
criteria.rationale: Competitive mechanics can create pressure unrelated to the chosen action.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Document whether leaderboards exist and how they can be avoided.

criteria.criterion: Collected data is described at the point it matters.
criteria.rationale: A plain-language explanation supports informed use and later review.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Map each core screen to the relevant privacy disclosure.

criteria.criterion: Deletion and account exit are discoverable.
criteria.rationale: A user should be able to leave without an opaque support maze.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Test the public and in-product deletion path.

criteria.criterion: Feature claims are separated from outcome claims.
criteria.rationale: A working feature does not by itself prove behavior change or health benefit.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Classify every material claim as feature, hypothesis or measured outcome.

criteria.criterion: Any outcome report states context, measures and limitations.
criteria.rationale: Without those details, a testimonial or metric cannot support a general conclusion.
criteria.evidencePrompt: Check the app version, period, sample, measure, attrition and comparison.

criteria.criterion: Medical or psychological claims have appropriate evidence and review.
criteria.rationale: Habit software should not imply treatment, diagnosis or guaranteed benefit without support.
criteria.evidencePrompt: List health-related wording and the evidence and review behind it.
